what_happened: While reading request 20261016-005805-p806, the reader (Athena's reading step) stopped at reading 1 and asked the user a question the repo and defaults did not settle. The request concerns the claude_version pin, which an agent runtime self-update can push out of date. The question was whether the pin should float or stay exact. The user answered: the pin stays exact, and whoever runs Athena bumps it after an update. Only one command should be added that sets claude_version to the installed version, and the refusal message should tell the operator to run it. No reading was wrong; the event was logged as a correction but was an answered question.
cause: Requests about a pin deadlock state the problem, not the policy that should govern it. Nothing in the defaults records stances such as exact pins versus floating ones, or who owns bumping them. The reading step has no way to settle such a policy choice before the job starts, so it surfaces as a question to the user. This differs from 85d6, which is about how to verify quality, and from 0hq0, which is about a fact the reader can't observe. Here the open point is a design preference the owner holds but that is not written down.
prevention: Add a written defaults entry for version pins and similar operator-owned config: pins stay exact, are never auto-floated, and are bumped by the operator through a single explicit command. That command sets the pin to the installed version, and any refusal caused by a mismatch names it. More broadly, the reading step should check a short list of recorded policy defaults before asking, and a policy choice the user answers should be added to that list. Then the whole class is answered from the defaults, not by asking the user each time.
proposed_request: Keep the claude_version pin exact; do not let it float. Add one command that sets claude_version in config to the version of the Claude runtime currently installed. Change the startup refusal that fires when the installed version differs from the pin so that it says plainly to run that command. Done when: (1) running the command on a mismatched install updates the pin to the installed version and a following agent start succeeds; (2) the refusal message names the command; (3) a test confirms that a mismatch still refuses and that the command clears it. Also record in the defaults that version pins stay exact and are bumped by the operator with a single command.
